summary: Los Padres NF lookout: built 1924 or 1929 (sources disagree), cab burned in 1977, restored by volunteers in 2019, and the chapter is running a $20,000 campaign to preserve it, with a full roof replacement now needed.

facts.design: steel-frame tower under a 13 x 13 ft cab; flat-roofed R-6 style cab since 1984

staffing.status: volunteer-staffed by the FFLA Monterey chapter
staffing.as_of: undated; chapter page refers to six years since the 2019 restoration

access.note: volunteer-staffed working lookout on Forest Service land; no public visiting program described in the sources

visit.trail_note: reached from Carmel Valley Road by about 9 miles of Forest Route 18S02 / Tassajara Road, most of it unpaved; high clearance needed on some stretches

events.note: a family lived in a government-owned cabin at the summit that also served as a fire lookout

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says the tower was built in 1924; Wikipedia says the current steel tower and cab were built in 1929 and mentions a 1919 summit cabin used as a lookout. No source read settles this, so the story presents both.
Wikipedia's text and NHLR describe a 12-foot tower, while Wikipedia's infobox gives a total height of 24 feet (7.3 m). The brief's 7.3 m matches the infobox figure and is kept as the total height.

sources.title: Monterey Chapter, Forest Fire Lookout Association

notes_for_editor: Construction date conflict (1924 NHLR vs 1929 Wikipedia) is unresolved; the brief's 1924 is kept with a note. Height 7.3 m is the Wikipedia infobox total, not the 12-ft tower. Staffing as_of is inferred from the chapter home page saying six years since the 2019 restoration; the page has no explicit date. Access marked restricted is an inference from the volunteer-run working lookout. No public visiting info found; current status in 2026 unverified beyond the chapter site.
